nodes.summary: For a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\langle\alpha\rangle\varphi$ is defined as $\alpha \to \bot$, that is, as $\neg[\alpha]\neg\varphi$: possibility is the dual of necessity.
nodes.title: Possibility in PDL

nodes.summary: The formulas of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atoms $p$, falsity $\bot$, implications $\varphi \to \psi$ of formulas, and boxes $[\alpha]\varphi$ of a program $\alpha$ and a formula $\varphi$. Formulas and programs are defined by simultaneous induction.
nodes.title: PDL formulas

nodes.summary: A model of propositional dynamic logic with set of worlds $W$ consists of a binary accessibility relation $R_a$ on $W$ for each atomic action label $a$, and a valuation that says which atoms are true at each world.
nodes.title: PDL model

nodes.summary: In a model $M$, each program $\alpha$ denotes a binary relation $R_\alpha$ on worlds: an atomic action $a$ denotes its accessibility relation $R_a$; $(w, v) \in R_{\alpha;\beta}$ iff $(w, u) \in R_\alpha$ and $(u, v) \in R_\beta$ for some world $u$; $R_{\alpha \cup \beta} = R_\alpha \cup R_\beta$; $R_{\alpha^*}$ is the reflexive-transitive closure of $R_\alpha$; and $(w, v) \in R_{\varphi?}$ iff $w = v$ and…
nodes.title: Relation denoted by a PDL program

nodes.summary: The programs of propositional dynamic logic over a type of atoms and a type of atomic action labels are the atomic actions $a$, sequential compositions $\alpha ; \beta$, nondeterministic choices $\alpha \cup \beta$, iterations $\alpha^*$, and tests $\varphi?$ of a formula $\varphi$. Programs and formulas are defined by simultaneous induction.
nodes.title: PDL programs

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha \cup \beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if both $[\alpha]\varphi$ and $[\beta]\varphi$ hold at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a choice

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, programs $\alpha$ and $\beta$, and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha;\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $[\alpha][\beta]\varphi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a sequential composition

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$, program $\alpha$ and formula $\varphi$, the formula $[\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ and $[\alpha][\alpha^*]\varphi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the box of an iteration

nodes.summary: For every model $M$, world $w$ and formulas $\psi$ and $\varphi$, the formula $[\psi?]\varphi$ holds at $w$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\psi$ holds at $w$.
nodes.title: Box of a test

nodes.summary: Truth of a formula at a world $w$ of a model $M$ is defined by recursion: an atom $p$ holds at $w$ iff the valuation of $M$ makes $p$ true at $w$; $\bot$ holds nowhere; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds at $w$ iff $\psi$ holds at $w$ whenever $\varphi$ does; and $[\alpha]\varphi$ holds at $w$ iff $\varphi$ holds at every world $v$ with $(w, v) \in R_\alpha$, where $R_\alpha$ is the relation denoted by $\alpha$ in $M$.
nodes.title: Satisfaction of PDL formulas

nodes.summary: The PDL model whose worlds are the two Booleans $\mathsf{true}$ and $\mathsf{false}$, with a single atomic action $a$ and a single atom $p$: the action $a$ relates each world $s$ exactly to its negation $\lnot s$, and $p$ holds exactly at $\mathsf{true}$.
nodes.title: The toggle model

nodes.summary: In the toggle model, with atomic action $a$ and atom $p$, the formula $[a;a]\,p$ is not satisfied at the world $\mathsf{false}$.
nodes.title: Failure of $(a;a)\,p$ in the toggle model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
